component.name: Simple Presenter
component.summary: Run ProPresenter presentations and media on a second screen

description.p: A simple, lightweight presenter for Linux that works on ProPresenter 7 folders as they are: its presentations, playlists and media. Slides go on a slide layer over a media layer, with shader transitions, on screens for the audience and for the stage.
It is a native application, made to run a show comfortably on modest and older computers. It is an independent project, not affiliated with Renewed Vision.

This is a personal experiment in vibe coding: it was built by describing it to an AI model, which wrote the code. It is shared as an example of what vibe coding can do in the hands of a hobby programmer, and is not a product for use. Nobody supports it, and it comes with no warranty of any kind.

ProPresenter's Text button, for the look of the words of every slide at once or of the slides selected with Ctrl and Shift; Apply This Text Style to All in a slide's menu; and the live slide drawn again on the screens when a theme or a text style is put on it.

Sound on many channels, routed as in ProPresenter: up to sixteen channels of the app's own, a Channel Routing matrix to the sound device's, and an Audio tab in the Media Inspector with ramps and each channel's routing and volume.
Smoother video under slide changes, as measured: a cut drawn once, and transitions, scrolling text and builds moving by each screen's own refreshes.
Screen Previews on a stage layout, and the preview in the operator window, changing by the screens' transitions, with switches for them; and a short guide behind a ? at the right of the toolbar.
A slide disabled by itself at a date set from its menu; and the editor's drags, a slider or a handle, taking half the work they did.

ProPresenter's Calendar, for events that take a presentation live or run a macro at their times; scrolling text; slides disabled and enabled from their menu; and a screen that goes to its display the first time it is turned on.

Playback markers on the transport, as flags over its bar that are dragged to move them and right-clicked to change them; and a marker changed while its media plays is where that media runs it from then on.

Playback markers: points in a video or a piece of audio whose actions run as playback reaches them, as ProPresenter's do. And the copyright display, which lays a song's copyright over its slides for a church's CCLI licence.

Next Cue: a video in a media playlist can go on to another of its playlist when it has played to its end, as ProPresenter's can. And tabs over the transport, which work the media layer's video, the announcements' video or the audio bin's music.

Video inputs: the computer's webcams and capture devices, live on a layer of their own under the media, with their sound, as ProPresenter's video inputs are. They are set up in Settings, shown from the media bin, by a slide or a macro, or as the fill of a shape.

One preview in the operator window, of whichever screen is picked under it, an audience screen or a stage screen with its layout and its Screen Previews, which can be dragged taller for a layout of several of them. The clear buttons are two columns of pictures beside it, as ProPresenter has them: the clear groups, and the layers in ProPresenter's order.

More actions for slides and macros, as ProPresenter has them: a playlist of the media bin or of the audio bin played from its start, left to play on when it is playing already unless the action's Always Retrigger is on; and a message shown with words of the action's own for its tokens. Each is picked from Add Action or dragged out of its list onto a slide or a macro.

Communication devices: a slide or a macro can send a MIDI note, a RossTalk Custom Control to a Ross switcher, or an HTTP request, and a MIDI device's notes work the show by ProPresenter's MIDI Map. They are set up in Settings, Devices, where ProPresenter's own devices for the workspace are offered.

ProPresenter's builds: the elements of a slide coming on one after another and going again, each with a transition of its own, With Slide, After Previous, With Previous or On Click, Next running the On Click ones before it goes on; the editor's Build tab for them, and for a theme's slides, whose builds a look runs on the screen it gives the theme; and a slide's own transition, or its presentation's, made in place of the one chosen.

ProPresenter's Media Inspector, for a slide's media, a row of the media bin and an element filled with a picture: the file, another in its place and a video's thumbnail from any moment; scaling, turning, flipping and cropping; how a video plays on and the part of it that plays; and ProPresenter's effects, drawn by shaders written for this app. And Quick Edit, for a slide's words put right over its thumbnail without the editor.

ProPresenter's HTTP API can be switched on, in the settings' Network section, so that what follows and operates ProPresenter over the network can be pointed at this instead: its state, its streams of changes, and what operates the show. What makes or changes things in the workspace's files is not there yet.

A screen can go out through an output of a Blackmagic DeckLink card, in one of ten formats, and an output that is a linked pair of connectors can key, internally or externally, with ProPresenter's alpha settings; tried so far on one card. Screens going out through cards are drawn together and handed over together, so that their outputs change together.

A shape can be filled with a Screen Preview, a picture of what one of the screens is showing, video and all, as ProPresenter's stage layouts have; and the benchmark measures what video and such a picture cost. Copy Text Style and Paste Text Style put the look of one slide's text boxes on another's. A paste into a text box keeps the box's own format and alignment. The slide live on the announcements has a green ring. A screen sent over NDI no longer goes out black after being switched off and on, and a song dressed in a theme keeps its chords.

Color Triggers for a text box linked to a timer: the time's words change colour as it comes down to given times, as in ProPresenter, with a list that can be dragged into order and kept as a default. Three public-domain Bibles come with the app. Bible mode reworked: a verse added before or after the passage keeps what is live as it is, the options in a panel, and Save and the verse buttons under the slides. Text boxes set to Single Line keep each word's look.

Bible mode: a passage typed is made into slides in a theme, with ProPresenter's Bible options, from a Bible imported as an XML file or read from api.bible a passage at a time; its words can be shared out evenly across the slides, broken where they pause. And the chord sheet as the Mac and Windows chord editors have it now: a line of hints, the line the pointer is on drawn in orange, and sharps and flats drawn as signs.

The announcements layer: a presentation can be sent to a layer of its own, over the slides, with its own clear button, while the show stays at the slide it was at. Go To Next timers on slides and a Slide Show for a whole presentation, by which slides go on by themselves. Masks, drawn in the editor and given to a screen in the Looks window. And a name typed where it stands in the editor's list.

The reflow editor: the slides' words as a table, for moving the words between slides. A slide is split in two where the caret is, the new slide being the slide over again with those words in it, and two slides are joined. The words keep their fonts, sizes, colours and chords through it.

The arrangement editor: a button over the slides opens two rows, the presentation's groups and the arrangement being viewed, and a group is dragged into the arrangement, along it, or taken out. Arrangements are made, copied, renamed and removed. The presentation's name is in the middle of the line over the slides.

Messages: named things to say over everything else, with tokens for a name, a room, the time of day or a timer, a theme to be drawn in, and a layer and a clear button of their own. The stage message, shown by the text boxes linked to it, which can flash as it comes. In the editor, a row of the list of a slide's elements is dragged up or down to change which element lies over which.

The audio bin, with a clear for the audio and a meter of how loud it is in the preview. A slide's notes, in a pane under the slide in the editor. What a text box shows is picked from one menu, and a slide's notes, the system clock and a video countdown are in it. In the chord editor, one of the key's chords can be dragged out of the strip onto a word.

The chord editors, as they came back from the editor that was made of them for the Mac and for Windows: the chord sheet's slides are a grid that zooms, each in a frame of its group's colour; a paste says what came of it; a song's two keys are over both editors; under them it says Autosave on, with Revert beside it; the ChordPro text has a size of its own; and the settings have the colour of a chord in each.

A slide by its number: type a slide's number while showing and it comes up over the slides; Enter takes that slide live, and a number left alone for a second goes away again. And Ctrl+, opens the settings.

A guard for a graphics driver that hangs when its video decoder is tried: on a computer whose NVIDIA card is run by the nouveau driver, without the firmware that driver's video decoder needs, video is now decoded by the processor, and a notice says so once. The settings have a part for video, where decoding can be kept to the processor on any computer, or the graphics chip's decoder tried whatever the app makes of the computer.

Clear groups, as ProPresenter has them: named sets of layers that are cleared together, at one click. Each of the workspace's groups has a button under the clears of the layers, and a right click on any clear button leads to the window they are set up in: the layers each clears, the picture on its button and a tint. F1 now clears the first group, which to begin with is Clear All, and an action on a slide or in a macro can clear a group.

From a slide's menu: Group puts the slide, and those after it in its group, into another group, and Label gives the slide a label, with a colour if wanted, from the labels the workspace keeps ready or made on the spot. A presentation can be renamed, which brings the playlists that have it along, and moved to the Trash. A box under the list of presentations narrows it to the names that have what is typed. And Simple View can keep the previews and the show controls at the right.

New presentations: the + beside Libraries makes a presentation in the library that is open, with a name of your choosing and one slide to start on. Until now a presentation could only be brought in from elsewhere.

Chords on a slide with no words: an intro or an instrumental made as an empty slide is on the chord editor's sheet, and in its ChordPro text, to be given chords. A chord with no words is now kept exactly as Multitracks keeps one. Nothing is added to a slide until a chord is put on it, and taking the chords off again leaves the slide as it was found.

Looks as ProPresenter has them: the live look by name in the toolbar, the Looks window with the screens across and the layers down, and a live look of its own that can be changed and saved. ProPresenter's own pictures on the buttons and the actions. And what an AI coding agent is told, so that it can help someone find out what is wrong on their own computer.
In the chord editor, a click on the next place keeps the chord that was being typed and starts the next one.
Chords: shown on the stage in any key, put on by hand in two editors, and brought in from ChordPro files.
Looks, which say what each audience screen gets; themes, to dress slides in; and search, by name or by words.
Setting a screen to NDI without NDI's library offers to fetch it, showing NDI's licence to be agreed to first.
The licence is now MIT. Nothing else is different from 0.6.
Up to sixteen screens, for the audience and for the stage, each sent to a window, a display or the network as an NDI source. The screens are kept awake while the show is on one.
A slide is shown before its actions are done, so a slide that clears itself is cleared, and is still marked as the live slide. A macro's colour is a block round its picture.

Slides and macros have actions: for timers, clearing, the stage, props and macros. They are added from a menu or by dragging, and those a ProPresenter presentation already has are run. Macros have a tab of their own. How a video plays on from its end (stop, loop, a number of times, for a length of time) is honoured, shown on the slide and changed from the slide. Menus that lead to more menus open them alongside. Props are shown a collection at a time and can be put in order by dragging.

The editor draws and makes shapes (rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, arrows) with colour, gradient and picture fills and feathered edges, turns elements, and adds, copies, pastes and deletes slides. Groups have hotkeys, kept where ProPresenter keeps them, and the slide a key goes to is marked. Show mode and edit mode have a button and a key each. Dragging a slider or a handle in the editor no longer falls behind the hand, and slides open and reach the output sooner. There is a benchmark for telling whether a change has made the app slower.

Simple View: the slides take the whole window, for seeing as many of them as will fit. A foreground video is played with its sound. Media can be dragged in from the file manager: onto a slide, between two slides, where it gets a slide of its own, or into the media bin. A video's thumbnail is a picture from a little way into it, not its first frame. The output and stage windows are kept out of Alt+Tab.

Media as a background or a foreground, with a transport for the video that is playing; timers, and text boxes that show them; props; stage layouts; text that scales to fit its box; and a log of each run, for working out what happened when something goes wrong.
The first release: showing presentations and media, playlists, and an editor for text boxes.
